caption:
Build a home gym with me (on a budget) ⤴️

Here’s the first few pieces I picked up to be able to workout as soon as possible

The main focus initially was around the basic essentials and a centerpiece rack that could function not only as a standard squat rack - but also as a fully functional adjustable cable machine. That way we could replicate almost everything you’d be gble to do in the gym, at home. 

Luckily @megastar.fitness has the perfect rack for that • Their P63 all in one power rack covered all of the bases and without having to spend an arm & leg (without skimping on quality)

Here’s everything we picked up initially:
- Barbell + pairs of bumper plates (5, 10, 15, 25, 35, 45 lks)
- Horse stall mats (10 pieces total)
- Sft x 5ft mirror
- P63 Power Rack (Megastar Fitness)
- Adjustable bench (Megastar Fitness)

Already had a set of PBs, a KB, and a few other pieces we were able to add to it for a solid start.

Not the lowest of low budgets, but I think this is right on the lower-middle end and most importantly - still keeping quality of items high. After all, this is ideally going to last you a long time. Making sure the main pieces will make it the distance is key 👍

caption:
Full Home Gym Tour! Cost breakdown is listed at the end of the caption.

How and why spend this much on a home gym set up?

How: I have accumulated this equipment over a 5 year period. The rack and wall panels are the only recent purchases. I have been saving and waiting to buy a functional trainer with the rack and cable set up for over 2 years. If you want to build something like this, start small, save, and formulate a plan to get there. If I can do it, anyone can. ��Why: I have a huge passion for exercise, it’s my hobby, favorite past time, and something I will do until the day I die. My wife loves lifting too. We want to instill that passion in our girls, and having this home gym set up allows us to do so by setting a great example. We also have very busy lives, so making our workout time as “frictionless” as possible is a major reason for having this set up at home. 

Here’s the full breakdown: $12,627
- Horse Stall Mats (Tractor Supply Co.) - $40 each, $640 total
